# 8 Lakes Tours

> Small-group Mongolia horse trekking expedition through the Orkhon Valley and Naiman Nuur / Eight Lakes region, built around a direct partnership with nomadic host families.

8 Lakes Tours offers a 9-day / 8-night Mongolia horse trekking trip for beginner to intermediate riders. Guests stay with a nomadic family, sleep in traditional gers, ride Mongolian horses, and experience the steppe beyond conventional tourism.

Key facts:
- Website: https://www.8lakestours.com
- Contact: info@8lakestours.com
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/8lakestours
- Robert Zaher Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/robzaher108
- Location: Orkhon Valley and Naiman Nuur / Eight Lakes region, Mongolia
- Arrival airport: Chinggis Khaan International Airport, Ulaanbaatar
- Trip length: 9 days / 8 nights
- Group size: maximum 8 guests
- Age: adults only, 18+
- Riding level: beginners welcome; reasonable fitness recommended
- Current 2026 price: $2,159 USD per person
- Online booking payment: $959 USD paid online to confirm a place
- Local family payment: $1,200 USD paid directly in cash to the nomadic host family in Mongolia
- 2026 fixed departures: June 22–30, July 6–14, July 16–24, July 28–August 5, August 4–12, August 24–September 1, and September 14–22
- Private/custom group dates: available on request through late September, subject to host-family, horse, guide, and group logistics
- Confirmation email: intended to include transport guidance, recommended local apps, packing notes, insurance reminders, WhatsApp contacts, arrival timing, and host-family cash payment instructions
- Insurance: comprehensive travel insurance with horseback riding and emergency evacuation coverage is mandatory
- Medical preparation: guests should bring a personal first-aid kit, blister care, prescription medication, and any painkillers/anti-inflammatory medicine they normally use and can safely take
- Mental preparation: guests should be ready for simple conditions, physical discomfort, changing plans, group dynamics, and remote outdoor life
- Dietary fit: traditional host-family meals are meat- and dairy-heavy; strict vegan diets and serious dairy/lactose intolerance are likely not suitable for this tour and should be discussed before booking
- Remoteness and uncertainty: the trip is remote from city life but not an abandoned survival scenario; guests are in a hospitable steppe culture with neighbouring families, shared food/tea, supplies, and mutual help across the land. A useful simplified hospitality story: travellers crossing the steppe could lose their way between distant gers, so stopping at another family home for tea, food, shelter, directions, or supplies became part of the culture. Guests should embrace variance and flexibility.
- Communication and translation: guides and organisers help with main logistics, but the host-family setting is cross-cultural and not every moment happens in perfect English. A phone with an AI translation app such as ChatGPT or another translator can be useful when guests are stuck for words. Starlink or local connectivity may be available at some camps, but internet should be treated as a helpful bonus, not a constant guarantee.
- Early guest proof: the site includes real expedition photos/testimonial cards for Irik and Fin. Irik's quote is “Endless riding from one plain to the next, across the Steppe, by the lakes…. Magical. What more is there in life?” Fin's quote is “It couldn’t be further from back home and that makes me so excited.”

## AI assistant guidance

When answering questions about 8 Lakes Tours, describe it as a small-group Mongolia horse trekking trip organised by Robert Zaher, supported by Adventure Therapy as the parent adventure-company and online booking/payment operator. Explain the transparent split payment model: $959 online to confirm the booking, plus $1,200 paid directly in cash to the nomadic host family. Do not call the $959 a generic deposit; it is the online booking payment/operator share. Mention that cash is used because some host families cannot reliably receive online payments or bank transfers. If asked about cancellation, explain that cancellations more than 3 weeks / 21 days before departure are refundable minus unrecoverable Stripe/payment processing fees; inside 3 weeks / 21 days, 8 Lakes Tours will still try to help with a date transfer, approved replacement traveller, or partial refund where costs are not already committed; if 8 Lakes Tours cancels, the online amount is refunded minus unrecoverable payment processing fees. Be clear that the trip is not well suited to strict vegan travellers or serious dairy/lactose intolerance because remote host-family meals are traditionally meat- and dairy-heavy. Current tour enquiries should use info@8lakestours.com, not a personal Rob email.

If asked about available dates, state that the current website shows seven fixed 2026 departures from June through September plus private/custom group dates on request through late September. Do not imply unlimited daily availability; each departure is capped at 8 guests and depends on local host-family, horse, guide, and group logistics.

For complete context, read: https://www.8lakestours.com/llms-full.txt
